answer: Atlas is showing value for CREATE SOMETHING: the business is mapped enough to reveal review signals, especially automation/database imbalance and worker/MCP concentration.

findings.title: Atlas is showing operating value
findings.summary: CREATE SOMETHING now has a connected internal map with all current topology records mapped and no hard gaps.
findings.nextAction: Use Atlas as the operating review surface instead of a static inventory; the value is in review-ready slices and proof-linked records.

findings.title: Automation is heavier than Database
findings.summary: Automation records substantially outnumber Database records. This is the clearest business-shape disconnect: execution has outrun the shared substrate.
findings.nextAction: Promote Substrate as the shared database layer so worker, MCP, agent, and policy surfaces read from the same source of truth.

findings.title: Worker surface concentration needs runtime ownership
findings.summary: Worker records are the largest runtime surface. This is not inherently bad, but it is where duplicated routes, configs, and deployment claims can hide.
evidence: Runtime binding coverage exists before production mutation
findings.nextAction: Review worker slices through runtime binding coverage and attach ownership, route, storage, and rollback proof before promotion.

findings.title: MCP surface overlap needs grouping
findings.summary: The MCP surface is large enough to be a product advantage and an operations risk. Similar MCP packages should be grouped by client, data domain, and runtime boundary.
evidence: MCP creation remains the strategic moat
findings.nextAction: Cluster MCP records by reusable capability versus client-specific adapter, then make each cluster API/MCP/agent addressable.

findings.title: Policy and guide knowledge is broad but needs attachment
findings.summary: Policy and guide records are well represented, but Atlas should keep pushing them onto the workflows they govern so docs do not become detached instructions.
findings.nextAction: Attach policy and guide nodes to the operating slices they govern, then treat missing attachment as a review signal.

recommendedMoves.title: Promote Substrate as the CREATE SOMETHING database layer
recommendedMoves.summary: The healthiest next move is to make the database layer a first-class product surface rather than a hidden app-governance implementation detail.
evidence: 25 Database records currently support 248 Automation records
Management surface exposes stable API/MCP/agent access
Atlas UI projects the same records instead of becoming a separate source of truth

recommendedMoves.title: Review worker runtime slices before production claims
recommendedMoves.summary: The worker surface is the largest concentration of operational risk and should be the first ongoing review lane.
evidence: 126 records in the primary worker slice

recommendedMoves.title: Turn client overlays into repeatable delivery
recommendedMoves.summary: Client overlays are mapped, which means CREATE SOMETHING can use itself as the proof path for client Atlas/Substrate implementations.
evidence: Client package surfaces are represented as Atlas/Substrate records

recommendedMoves.title: Attach policy and guides to operating slices
recommendedMoves.summary: Policy is already present; the improvement is to make every critical workflow show its policy, guide, approval boundary, and receipt path in context.
